title: ChatDesign: Bootstrapping Generative Floor Plan Design With Pre-trained Large Language Models
task: 交互式平面图生成与编辑
inputData: 自然语言需求及多种用户交互（文本、语音、点击、拖拽），统一转换为标准化操作与几何参数
contribution: 提出ChatDesign，将预训练大语言模型用于自然语言驱动的平面图生成，并通过统一指令翻译器将不同交互形式映射为Locate、Move、Resize、Add和Delete等结构化操作，实现迭代生成与局部编辑。
abstract: ChatDesign uses a pre-trained large language model and decoder to generate floor-plan regression parameters from natural-language descriptions and supports iterative refinement through user feedback. It also integrates multiple interaction modalities through standardized editing operations.
methodology: The workflow uses a pre-trained LLM to process natural-language floor-plan requirements and a decoder to produce regression parameters and floor-plan outputs. Iterative refinement incorporates the original text, previous results, and subsequent user feedback. A Uniform Instructions Translator normalizes text, audio, mouse-click, and drag-and-drop interactions into five core operations—Locate, Move, Resize, Add, and Delete—with explicit object, position, and dimension parameters so the same downstream editing mechanism can handle different interaction modalities.
results: On the main benchmark, ChatDesign achieved Micro-IoU 58.31 and Macro-IoU 55.43, compared with 54.34 and 53.30 for Tell2Design and 64.67 and 62.32 for human designers. The iterative variant achieved Micro-IoU 54.57 and Macro-IoU 57.24. On 10 challenging Tell2Design examples, ChatDesign reached Micro-IoU 56.82 and Macro-IoU 60.56 versus Tell2Design's 47.56 and 51.10, showing roughly a 10% improvement after interactive refinement. Visual comparisons also show generated layouts approaching the ground-truth and human-designed plans.
taskEn: Interactive floor plan generation and editing
inputDataEn: Natural-language requirements and multimodal user interactions (text, voice, clicks, and drag-and-drop), normalized into structured operations and geometric parameters
operationEvidence: ChatDesign generates floor-plan parameters/designs from user requirements and implements Locate, Move, Resize, Add, and Delete operations that modify an existing floor-plan state through explicit operation parameters.
